findings.summary: parseCompose lacks a counterpart to normalizeDraft's MAX_ITEMS cap, allowing an authenticated caller to post a large compose file that can block the event loop and produce an unbounded draft.
findings.scenario: An authenticated user posts a 60,000-character compose file declaring thousands of services. The server processes this request synchronously, performing a near-miss scan that is O(proposed entities x workspace roster) and re-parses the entire draft when any item matches an existing entity. This can block the event loop for seconds, resulting in a draft that no reviewer can work through.
